revisions.title: Law as a second-best imitation
revisions.body: The Stranger presents law as a second-best imitation of expert rule. Written rules imitate truth, and a regime without the genuine expert should follow its written laws and ancestral customs as closely as it can. The passage poses departure for private gain or favor, by someone acting without knowledge, as a worse error. Law therefore preserves a likeness of expertise without becoming expertise itself.
